question: A function \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by \(\displaystyle f(x)=\begin{cases}e^{-1/x},&x>0,\\0,&x\le0.\end{cases}\) Then

options.B: \(f\) is differentiable but \(f^\prime\) is not continuous
options.C: \(f\) is continuous but \(f^\prime(0)\) does not exist
